problems.problem: A set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is called irregular if for any two distinct elements $x,y\in A$, the set $A$ contains no other element of the form $x+k(y-x)$ where $k\in\mathbb Z$. Does there exist an infinite irregular set?

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Suppose that the sum of the matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_n\in\mathbb R^{n	imes n}$ is the identity matrix but $\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i A_i$ is singular whenever at least one of the coefficients $\alpha_i\in\mathbb R$ is zero.

(a) Show that $\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i A_i$ is non-singular provided that $\alpha_i
e0$ for all $i$.

(b) Prove that if the matrices $A_i$ are symmetric, then each has rank $1$.

Let $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfy the following: it is linear between adjacent integers, and for $n=0,1,\ldots$, $$f(n)=\begin{cases}0&\text{if }2\mid n,\\4^\ell+1&\text{if }2\nmid n,\ 4^{\ell-1}\le n<4^\ell\ (\ell=1,2,\ldots).\end{cases}$$ Let $f^1(x)=f(x)$, and $f^k(x)=f(f^{k-1}(x))$ for all integers $k\ge2$. Determine $\liminf_{k\to\infty}f^k(x)$ and $\limsup_{k\to\infty}f^k(x)$ for Lebesgue almost every $x\in[0,\infty)$.

For each polynomial $f$ of degree $n$ with integer coefficients, consider the integral $$\int_{-1}^1x^nf(x)\,dx.$$ Let $\alpha_n$ denote the smallest positive real number that can be obtained as the value of such an integral. Determine $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log\alpha_n}{n}.$$
Is it possible to select a non-degenerate segment from every line in the plane in such a way that they are pairwise disjoint?
Let $\varepsilon$ be a primitive $7$th root of unity. Determine all integers of the form $|\alpha|^2$ for some element $\alpha$ of the cyclotomic field $\mathbb Q(\varepsilon)$.

There are chess pieces located on each vertex of a regular $k$-gon. We are allowed to pick up a piece and move it to the point obtained by reflecting its current position to that of another piece. By repeatedly performing this type of move, for what integers $k\ge3$ are we able to achieve a situation where all pieces once again occupy the vertices of a regular $k$-gon, but the polygon is of different size than the original?

Prove that for a suitable choice of the signs $\varepsilon_n=\pm1$ the function $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\varepsilon_n}{n^s}:\{\operatorname{Re}s>1\}\to\mathbb C$ accumulates to every complex number at every point $\xi\in\{\operatorname{Re}s=1\}$ (i.e. for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and $\xi\in\{\operatorname{Re}s=1\}$ there exists a sequence $s_n\to\xi$, $\operatorname{Re}s_n>1$ such that $f(s_n)\to z$).

Consider the group formed by the vectors in the plane under addition. Suppose a set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ contains a Borel subset of a circular arc that has positive linear measure. Show that $S$ is a generating set of the above group.
Does there exist a continuous function $f:\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q\to\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$ such that the preimage of each irrational number is of positive Hausdorff dimension?
